← SOLSTICE PROJECT NOTES

Next decisions — digital reconstruction and fitment, P5

This plan is for the digital modeling objective. No physical pan measurement, mock-up, coupon, bench test or engine test is a prerequisite to continuing or completing this work. The preserved physical measurement/test plan is available at ../history/NEXT_DECISIONS_PHYSICAL_PLAN_2026-10-13.md if a later build is separately requested.

What digital fitment means here

Build the most accurate editable Solstice GXP pan and insert model supported by available sources, then test each concept against explicitly named reconstructed scenarios. A virtual pass means clearance against those stated digital surfaces and ranges. It does not convert an image-derived or assumed surface into exact OEM geometry, and does not claim fit to a particular physical pan.

The firm dimensional anchor is the published GM 12601240 overall maximum envelope: 474.7 × 316 × 117.99 mm (GM product specification). Catalog and service sources identify the Solstice pan/cover/baffle family, five baffle fasteners, pickup topology, and related fastener identities. They do not supply the hidden cavity, cover relief, pickup envelope, boss coordinates, seat heights or an installed-car transform. No matching 12601240 CAD model or dimensioned internal drawing surfaced in the recorded search.

The source-view/camera audit now records observed correspondences and adopts an exterior-only shallow-shelf relief. It does not narrow any interior fit parameter or justify coupling the existing stress cases.

Current options and variables to keep in view

  • A — simple gated well: fewest current custom gates; directional retention and refill area remain design hypotheses.
  • B — radial collector: diagonal gates and guide vanes broaden the collection directions; larger envelope and more seams.
  • C — nested reservoir: two stages and six gates test buffering; largest part count/envelope and most complex refill path.
  • Historical alternatives: fixed dividers and purchased-gate proxies stay available for comparison; purchased proxy geometry is not supplier CAD.

Across the options, inspect horizontal footprint and rotation, vertical height, floor step, wall/floor bypass, cover and rotating keepouts, pickup/screen/tube envelope, drain/return/vent paths, gate opening/closing direction, independent gate poses, removal path, cleanliness/service access, material thickness, part count, mass, process features, and sensitivity to parameter changes. Treat oil viscosity, available head, acceleration/gravity cases, oil inventory and flow as separate physical phenomena: CAD area/volume is only geometry, not a flow or starvation prediction.

Digital completion criteria

The digital candidate is complete when the named source evidence and assumptions are traceable; the editable pan/cover/pickup/insert assemblies are inspectable; A/B/C are compared in common frames and declared digital scenarios; interference and motion checks cover the stated poses and surfaces; source STEP/DXF profiles and BOMs agree; animations are visibly illustrative; and the review page says what is source-backed, inferred and unknown. Any unbounded hidden interface remains visibly uncertain instead of blocking the digital deliverable.

Physical manufacture, installation, service life and oil-pressure performance are outside this digital completion criterion. If a later physical build is requested, the existing QUALITY.md fabrication and engine-use checks apply as a separate release decision.
